messages.subject: Moderated mediation with latent variables
parts:
Dear all, 

I am trying to run a moderated mediation analysis on latent variables in lavaan. Mediation part is pretty straightforward, but I am stuck with the moderation analyses and I don't know how to put everything together.

I found some resources regarding indProd function (in this group) and I tried to create product terms  of IV (measured via 8 items) and moderator variable (measured via 10 items), here is the syntax I have used:

dataind <-indProd(f_mod_data, var1=c("x1","x2","x3", "x4", "x5",
                                 "x6", "x7", "x8"),
                 var2=c("w1","w2","w3", "w4", "w5", "w6",
                        "w7", "w8", "w9", "w10"), match = FALSE, meanC = TRUE,
                 residualC = FALSE, doubleMC = FALSE)

As a result, now I have almost 80 new variables which represent combinations of my IV and moderator variable items and I am not sure what to do next and how to add these variables to my sem model. I was hoping to get one variable containing interaction term, which I could use further to conduct moderated mediation. 

Any thoughts how to solve this problem or any suggestions what am I doing wrong? 

Thanks, 

Nino

messages.author: 9a8f7a9bed77c44a
messages.subject: Re: Moderated mediation with latent variables
parts:
All possible combinations were produced (10*8 =80). You should use an equal number of indicators for each latent variable and use `match = T`. If you use three indicators per factor you will get 3 new indicators (for the latent moderation variable; e.g. x1.x4, x2.x5, x3.x6) with which you should create the measurement model for the latent moderation factor.

Also check `help("indProd")`.

On Friday, October 16, 2020 at 9:02:25 PM UTC+4 Fran wrote:
If you use  match=T the number of variables in all sets must be equal. 

I'd do this first
library (dplyr)
df %<>%
  rowwise %>%
  mutate(w7_8= mean(c(w7, w8)),
         w9_10= mean(c(w9, w10))) %>%
  ungroup

Check with f_mod_data$,you will find two new variables, w7_8 and w9_10.
Your moderator is now composed by w1, w2, w3,  w4,  w5,  w6, w7_8, w9_10.
So you have equal numbers of variables (8 each) and you can use match=T

df<-indProd(f_mod_data, var1 = c ("w1", "w2", "w3", "w4", "w5", "w6", "w7_8", "w9_10"), 
                var2 = c ("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7", "x8"),
                           match=T)

In your SEM model create the new latent variable using the result from  indProd, it should be something like this:

anyName=~ w1.x1 + w2.x2 + w3.x3 + [...] + w9_10.x8

Fran

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Moderated mediation with latent variables
parts:
Saying "it doesn't work" doesn't give us much to go on. What errors or warnings are you getting?

One thing is here:

# direct effect
             Y ~ c*X + w*W + aw*mod
           # mediator
             M ~ a*X + w*W + aw*mod
             Y ~ b*M + w*W + aw*mod

By giving the same labels (w and aw) to the W and mod regressors in all three equations, you're constraining those regression coefficients to equality (e.g., the effect of W on M is the same as the effect of W on Y), which is probably not what you want. You also have W and mod predicting Y in two different equations. Try something like:

             M ~ a*X + wm*W + awm*mod
             Y ~ c*X + b*M + wy*W + awy*mod

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Moderated mediation with latent variables
parts: 1) I should I use double mean centering instead of mean centering in indProd?
From my reading of the source material, you should use double-mean-centering instead of mean-centering in any situation.
2) Should I center predictor items and moderator items as well? or will it suffice to double mean center their interaction term only?

Double-mean-centering involves 2 steps (automated by indProd()):
  1. mean-center indicators of both factors before calculating product indicators
  2. mean-center the product indicators

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
